title: The Firstborn
lead: The first son held a special place in the family and, in Israel, belonged to God. The theme runs from Esau's birthright and the death of Egypt's firstborn to Christ, "the firstborn of all creation" (Colossians 1:15).

sections.b: Genesis often passes over the firstborn: Abel's offering is accepted over Cain's (Genesis 4), Isaac is chosen over Ishmael, Jacob receives the birthright and blessing over Esau (Genesis 25:29–34; 27), Ephraim is set before Manasseh (Genesis 48:13–20), and Reuben loses his place (Genesis 49:3–4). God's choice does not follow birth order.

God calls Israel his firstborn son (Exodus 4:22). Because Israel's firstborn were spared at Passover, they belong to the LORD (Exodus 13:2; Numbers 8:17). The Levites take their place in God's service, and five shekels are paid for each firstborn beyond their number (Numbers 3:11–13, 40–51; 18:15–16). Deuteronomy protects the firstborn's double share even when a father prefers another wife's son (Deuteronomy 21:15–17).
sections.refs: Exodus 4:22; Exodus 13:2; Numbers 3:11–13; Numbers 3:40–51; Numbers 8:17; Numbers 18:15–16; Deuteronomy 21:15–17

sections.h: The firstborn in the New Testament
sections.b: The king of Psalm 89:27 is made God's "firstborn, the highest of earth's kings." The New Testament gives Jesus this title: Mary's firstborn (Luke 2:7, 22–23), "firstborn of all that was created" and "firstborn from the dead" (Colossians 1:15, 18), "the firstborn among many brothers" (Romans 8:29). Hebrews speaks of "the gathering of the firstborn" enrolled in heaven (Hebrews 12:23).
sections.refs: Psalm 89:27; Luke 2:7; Luke 2:22–23; Romans 8:29; Colossians 1:15–18; Hebrews 1:6; Hebrews 12:23
